title: Domain Event envelope
description: Machine-readable Domain Event envelope contract: stable metadata shared by persistent domain-event records (docs/architecture/events.md). Envelope baseline plus the G3 runtime scope contract (ADR-0022): optional execution_id, attempt_id, attempt_outcome with conditional per-family validation. The canonical G2 mutation taxonomy (ADR-0021, events.md section 4.1) plus the three runtime types (ADR-0022, events.md section 4.2) are listed as event_type examples: nine lifecycle types plus project.created, task.created, task.dependency_added, execution.created, attempt.created, attempt.concluded. No payload taxonomy, no persistence encoding, no ordering or general provenance envelope beyond the runtime scope decided here.
$comment: Persisted-fact envelope, not RPC: the schema describes committed facts and contains no execution-request fields. Schema-valid JSON != authoritative event: a model/provider cannot mint domain history by matching this shape; only trusted validated application services commit Event Journal facts. SECRET values must not enter journal payloads (INV-008); JSON Schema cannot prove data classification from arbitrary strings, so no fake regex security is attempted here — enforcement is Policy/application responsibility. additionalProperties is intentionally permissive so future domain-specific event data can extend this baseline once taxonomy is decided. event_type stays an open string (no enum) so the envelope never becomes a closed registry; the examples array records the canonical G2 + G3-runtime names without enforcing them. Runtime scope convention: a scope field that must be absent on an event family is constrained to null (absent and explicit-null are equivalent); from_state/to_state remain TaskState semantics and are null on all runtime events; attempt_outcome serializes the agent-runtime AttemptOutcome as succeeded/failed/timed_out/cancelled (lowercase, distinct from SCREAMING Task states). This schema selects no Event Journal serialization encoding and introduces no Event Sourcing. See docs/architecture/events.md for semantics.

event_type.description: Typed event identity as non-empty string. Open vocabulary (no enum): exact naming convention for future types remains open, but the canonical G2 mutation names and the three G3 runtime names in examples are stable. Typed Agent Bus names, FakeAgent scenario names, and provider-specific types must not be read in here.

schema_version.description: Event-record schema version. Distinct from application build version, IPC protocol version, and provider version. No upcasting or deprecation policy is defined here.

occurred_at.description: Serialized timestamp representation only. Clock source, precision, monotonic ordering, and generation origin remain open implementation items.

correlation_id.description: Identifier of the larger operation/workflow/execution chain this fact belongs to. Format remains open; correlation != causation.

causation_id.description: Identifier of the prior action/event/request that directly caused this fact. Format remains open; causation != correlation.

task_id.description: Task aggregate reference. Null only for project.created; required in practice for every other canonical family (scope matrix in events.md section 4.2).

project_id.description: Project aggregate reference: the root scope. Required in practice for every canonical family.

from_state.description: Task lifecycle state before the mutation. TaskState semantics only; null on project.created and on all runtime events (runtime outcomes never live here).

to_state.description: Task lifecycle state after the mutation. TaskState semantics only; null on project.created and on all runtime events.

execution_id.description: Execution aggregate reference (ADR-0022). Null on every G2 family; non-blank string on every runtime fact. Never encoded into reason, provenance, or correlation/causation fields.

attempt_id.description: Attempt aggregate reference (ADR-0022). Null on every G2 family and on execution.created; non-blank string on attempt.created and attempt.concluded.

attempt_outcome.description: Canonical terminal Attempt outcome (ADR-0022): the agent-runtime AttemptOutcome serialized lowercase (Succeeded->succeeded, Failed->failed, TimedOut->timed_out, Cancelled->cancelled). Required only on attempt.concluded; null everywhere else, including all G2 events.
